title: Differentials of an arbitrary symmetric algebra
statement: Let R be a commutative ring and K an arbitrary R-module. Put S=Sym_R(K) with generator map iota:K -> S [lem-weil-pbc-symmetric-algebra-universal-property]. There exists an S-linear equivalence e:Omega[S/R] -> S tensor_R K such that e(d(iota(k)))=1 tensor k for every k in K. Here differentials are as in [def-weil-pbc-kahler-differentials] and extension of scalars is as in [lem-weil-pbc-module-base-change-universal-property]. This holds without finite generation, freeness or projectivity of K.

source.place: Tags 00DM and 00RO; the symmetric-algebra differential calculation used in Tag 07M7; parent node proof step 2

proof.text: For any S-module N and R-linear v:K -> N, use SymmetricAlgebra.lift on k -> (iota(k),v(k)) into the trivial square-zero extension S plus N. The first component is the identity by SymmetricAlgebra.algHom_ext. The second component d_v is an R-derivation by the square-zero multiplication law, and d_v(iota(k))=v(k). Two derivations agreeing on iota(K) agree on constants, sums and products by the derivation laws, and therefore on all S by SymmetricAlgebra.induction.

For N=S tensor_R K and v(k)=1 tensor k, lift d_v through the differential universal property to f:Omega[S/R] -> S tensor_R K. Extend the R-linear map k -> d(iota(k)) to g:S tensor_R K -> Omega[S/R]. The composite g f composed with d agrees with d on iota(K), so derivation uniqueness and differential universality give g f=id. The composite f g is the identity on 1 tensor k, so base-change extensionality gives f g=id. Form the linear equivalence with forward map f and inverse g; its required generator formula follows from d_v(iota(k))=1 tensor k.

lean.statement:
theorem symmetric_algebra_differentials
    (R K : Type u) [CommRing R] [AddCommGroup K] [Module R K] :
    ∃ e : KaehlerDifferential R (SymmetricAlgebra R K) ≃ₗ[SymmetricAlgebra R K]
        (SymmetricAlgebra R K ⊗[R] K),
      ∀ k : K, e (KaehlerDifferential.D R (SymmetricAlgebra R K)
        (SymmetricAlgebra.ι R K k)) = 1 ⊗ₜ[R] k
